La propuesta de esta guía es resolverlo como ataque cuerpo a cuerpo apuntado a la cabeza, aplicando sus reglas; Disparo certero no elimina el penalizador de un ataque cuerpo a cuerpo apuntado.

5. Peligros y reglas que se activan durante Hallt

Combate, protección y heridas

Un turno concede normalmente un Movimiento y una Acción, por orden de Iniciativa. En cuerpo a cuerpo se comparan NE; daño del arma + diferencia de NE, menos BR y armadura de la ubicación. La ubicación suele obtenerse invirtiendo los dados del ataque. Dobles exitosos pueden causar críticos y dobles fallidos, pifias. Llegar a 0 Heridas no equivale a morir: consulta Heridas críticas y sus consecuencias.

En Hallt, Armadura 2 (8) significa 2 puntos de armadura y 8 de protección total con BR. No restes 8 y luego BR otra vez. El daño de los rasgos Arma, Mordisco y Tentáculo ya lleva su componente de Fuerza: no la añadas de nuevo.

Frío, oscuridad y estados

Quedarse al raso requiere considerar exposición al frío y Fatigado; el suplemento remite al manual, p. 181. En el Sapo Tranquilo, aceptar comida y bebida permite eliminar la Fatiga del viaje según la escena. Las velas, lámparas y Luz importan: Borin y Felix tienen Visión nocturna, que necesita al menos luz tenue, no oscuridad absoluta.

Ten a mano Ardiendo, Tumbado, Enmarañado y Quebrantado. Ardiendo causa al final del asalto 1d10 de daño, +1 por cada estado adicional, reducido por BR y la menor armadura disponible, mínimo 1; Atletismo puede eliminar estados según los NE. Enmarañado impide moverse y penaliza las acciones que requieren movimiento: los tentáculos del engendro lo hacen especialmente peligroso.

Miedo y Terror

Miedo (nivel) exige una prueba prolongada de Frialdad hasta reunir tantos NE como su nivel. Puede repetirse al final de los asaltos. Mientras persista, −1 NE a pruebas para afectar a la fuente; acercarse exige Frialdad +0 y, si ella se acerca, Frialdad +0 o Quebrantado.

Terror exige una prueba inicial de Frialdad, con dificultad fijada por el DJ. Fallar causa tantos estados de Quebrantado como nivel de Terror + NE negativos. Después la criatura causa Miedo del mismo nivel. Ejemplo con dificultad +0: Otto tiene Frialdad 42 y saca 67 (−2 NE) ante Terror 2: sufre 4 estados de Quebrantado.

Persecuciones

Fija una Distancia inicial y pide Atletismo, Montar o Conducir según el caso. Compara el peor NE de los perseguidos con el mejor de los perseguidores y modifica la Distancia por la diferencia: a 0 o menos hay alcance; a 10 o más, fuga. Ejemplo: Distancia 4, perseguido +1 y perseguidor +3: baja a 2. Estas dificultades las determina el DJ, no son pruebas numéricas adicionales prescritas por Hallt.

Sanar

Fuera de combate, Peter usa Sanar 49: un 26 da +2 NE y cura BI 3 +2 = 5 Heridas. La curación de Heridas mediante Sanar se limita a una vez por paciente y encuentro. En combate, su talento Primeros auxilios concede su NE vinculado al tener éxito; además permite invertir un fallo al usar vendas si así obtiene éxito, limitado entonces a +1 NE.

Corrupción

Ante una influencia corruptora, el DJ pide Aguante +0 para exposición física o Frialdad +0 para espiritual. Para exposición moderada: fallo, 2 puntos; éxito con 0–1 NE, 1 punto; éxito con 2 o más, ninguno. Gerda, Aguante 43, obtiene 21 (+2 NE): evita la Corrupción de esa exposición. Aplica el desencadenante de la influencia o del rasgo, no una tirada por cada mirada al enemigo.

La catástrofe final del suplemento tiene consecuencia propia: todos los situados en una milla reciben 3 puntos de Corrupción. No la rebajes a una exposición ordinaria. Si el total de Corrupción supera BV + BR, entra en juego la prueba de Aguante para evitar mutación. Revisa talentos aplicables, como Alma pura, antes de calcular el umbral individual.

Fortuna, Destino y Resolución

Fortuna permite repetir una prueba fallida, añadir +1 NE a una prueba o elegir cuándo actuar en el asalto según las reglas. Destino se sacrifica para evitar la muerte. Resolución puede dar inmunidad a Psicología hasta el final del siguiente asalto. Son recursos distintos de Ventaja, también útiles en una partida corta. El suplemento propone expresamente la intervención del jinete al salvar a alguien con Destino en la granja.

Los valores siguientes proceden del PDF español. Se indican las características usadas cuando una habilidad básica no figura entrenada. Un «ejemplo +0» es una situación ilustrativa: el DJ sigue aplicando alcance, visibilidad, estados, Estatus y demás circunstancias. No es una nueva dificultad impuesta por la aventura.

Goswin Samter · jurista

Carisma 65, Sobornar 65, Derecho 67, Teología 53, Percepción 40, Consumir alcohol 55. Para huir sin avances: Atletismo con Agilidad 30; para resistir miedo, Frialdad con Voluntad 55.

Parloteo 1: Carisma enfrentada a Inteligencia para aturullar. En éxito añade +1 NE por el talento; impone 1 Aturdido más otro por su nivel: 2 estados con una adquisición. El objetivo embobado solo intenta seguir sus palabras. No lo apliques a toda conversación o negociación.

Ejemplo +0: Carisma 65, tirada 32: +3 NE, o +4 NE si es Parloteo. Enfrenta ese resultado a la Inteligencia del interlocutor. Para una cuestión jurídica, Derecho 67 y tirada 35 dan +3 NE.

Daga de plata: daño publicado +6; BR 4, sin armadura indicada. Su función habitual es hablar, pagar y buscar protección; combatir es un último recurso.

Hallt, p. 7. Perfil original de Foundry.

Gismondo · el jinete sin cabeza

Cuerpo a cuerpo (básico) 85, Arrojadiza 66, Intimidar 78, Montar (caballo) 55, Movimiento silencioso (rural) 60. Defensa cuerpo a cuerpo 85; Esquivar sin avances usa Agilidad 39. Frialdad sin avances usa Voluntad 48.

Jinete experto 1: ordena una Acción a Hel sin prueba de Montar; cuando sí corresponda Montar en combate, añade +1 NE a un éxito. Maestro del combate 2: cuando esté superado en número cuenta como dos personas adicionales para calcular superioridad numérica. Aterrador 1: puede causar Miedo 1.

Mientras va montado: contra un adversario menor que Hel, obtiene +20 al ataque cuerpo a cuerpo: básico 85 pasa a 105, antes de otros modificadores. Un rival que ataque al jinete, menor que su montura, sufre −10. Su Esquivar 39 se reduce a 19 por el −20 de ir montado: Jinete experto no sustituye a Equitación acrobática. Utiliza Movimiento 7 de Hel y Montar para correr o saltar. Son las reglas de combate montado del manual, no el sistema opcional completo de ¡A las armas!.

Empuñar dos armas 1: requiere llevar ambas armas. Usa la tirada de la mano principal y, si impacta, su inversión para la secundaria, con −20 por mano torpe; cada golpe tiene defensa propia. Suma el NE vinculado al talento en pruebas exitosas de ese uso. Hasta su siguiente turno, −10 a sus defensas. Solo genera Ventaja por este uso si acierta ambos golpes.

Ejemplo de dos armas +0: con habilidad 85, un 34 da +5 NE y +1 del talento = +6. Si impacta, el segundo usa 43 contra 65 (85 −20): +2 NE y +1 = +3. Compara cada uno con una defensa nueva. El daño del hacha es +10; el de una espada de mano ordinaria sería BF 6 +4 = +10.

Disparo certero elige ubicación con armas a distancia, incluidas las bombas cuando corresponda, no con el hacha. Recio ya está reflejado en sus 20 Heridas. Tiene 2 Destino y 2 Fortuna. Los impactos a su cabeza se ignoran.

Hacha de verdugo: usa Cuerpo a cuerpo (básico); daño +10, Impactante al emplearla desde posición elevada, como montado. Si causa un crítico en la cabeza, tira dos veces y elige el peor resultado para la víctima. Armadura 2 (8). Con Intimidar 78, un 42 da +3 NE antes de la oposición.

En el primer ataque de Hel, el suplemento pide evitar críticos contra los PJ. Cuando Gismondo pase de neutral a aliado efectivo, cambia la reserva de Ventaja a la que contribuye.

Hallt, pp. 8–9. Perfil original de Foundry.

Hel · montura del jinete

HA publicada 45, Fuerza 55, Resistencia 45, Agilidad 30, Voluntad 15, Movimiento 7. Sus pruebas habituales son ataques con HA, oposición física con Fuerza y maniobras con su jinete. No tiene una habilidad de Montar: esa prueba es de Gismondo.

Adiestrado (Montura, Guerra, Magia): acepta jinete, está entrenada para combatir y no se espanta por magia. Guerra aporta +10 HA e ignora Asustadizo por ruidos fuertes; al usar un perfil preparado, comprueba si ese +10 ya está incorporado antes de añadirlo. Los ejemplos de esta guía conservan la HA 45 publicada como valor de mesa.

Grande: Miedo 1 frente a tamaño Normal si es agresiva; sus ataques obtienen Dañina y quien la pare con Cuerpo a cuerpo sufre −2 NE por diferencia de tamaño. Esquivar evita ese penalizador. En Fuerza enfrentada, un oponente Normal necesita un crítico para poder comparar NE con ella.

Ejemplo: ataque contra 45, tirada 23: +2 NE antes de la defensa y las cualidades. Arma +7 ya incluye Fuerza. Armadura 2 (6), 23 Heridas. Zancada multiplica Carrera por 1,5: con Movimiento 7, Carrera 28 pasa a 42 yardas.

Hallt, p. 9; manual, Adiestrado, Tamaño y Zancada. Perfil original de Foundry.

Markolf Bachmaye · cervecero

Carisma 55, Consumir alcohol 55, Pelea 49, Oficio (cervecero) 40, Percepción 40, Saber local 50. Frialdad no entrenada usa Voluntad 40; Esquivar, Agilidad 30; Atletismo para huir, Agilidad 30.

Juerguista 1: +1 NE en éxitos de Consumir alcohol y de Carisma/Cotilleo en fiestas. Además puede invertir una tirada fallida de Consumir alcohol si la inversión la convierte en éxito.

Ejemplo: Consumir alcohol 55, tirada 73: puede invertir a 37, éxito de +2 NE, más 1 por Juerguista = +3 NE. Carisma 55 con 24 da +3 NE, o +4 NE en un contexto festivo. No gana ese NE al resistir con Frialdad las sospechas de los PJ.

Condenado es su destino narrativo, no un modificador genérico. Puño americano +7; cuero en el cuerpo 1 (6), BR 5 fuera de esa ubicación. 18 Heridas. Si sobrevive al ataque, usa la prueba de Carisma de los PJ descrita en la escena para calmarlo.

Hallt, pp. 12 y 14. Perfil original de Foundry.

Elva Fellgiebel · alguacil y líder de la secta

Carisma 65, Sobornar 52, Frialdad 67, Percepción no entrenada 54, Intimidar 39, Cuerpo a cuerpo (básico) 53, Esquivar 48. Para su especialización mágica: Hablar idioma (magia) 74, Canalización 66, Sabiduría académica (Dhar) 72.

Cerebro conserva respetabilidad al ignorar la pérdida de Estatus de Delincuente; no aumenta Inteligencia ni concede un NE universal. Aterrador permite Miedo 1. Magia menor y su Saber arcano oscuro explican la lista de hechizos publicada.

Ejemplos +0: Carisma 65, tirada 32: +3 NE para persuadir; Frialdad 67, tirada 35: +3 NE para mantener la compostura; Saber (Dhar) 72, tirada 46: +3 NE. Contra sospechas de los PJ utiliza la oposición apropiada a lo que intentan, no una mentira automáticamente exitosa por su cargo.

Hechizos publicados: Dardo, Drenar, Escuchar, Escudo mágico, Explosión, Manifestar demonio menor y Sangre corrosiva. Los tres primeros tienen NL 0; Escudo mágico, Explosión y Sangre corrosiva, NL 4; Manifestar demonio menor, NL 8 según los registros de hechizo exportados.

Ejemplo de lanzamiento: con Hablar idioma (magia) 74, un 32 da +4 NE: alcanza NL 4 sin canalizar. Un 52 da +2 NE y basta para NL 0, pero no para NL 4. En Dardo, su BV 6 +4 NE causa 10 de Daño antes de protección. Drenar necesita además toque enfrentado si el objetivo se resiste: utiliza Pelea sin avances con HA 46; ignora armadura y la cura 1 Herida.

Canalización es una prueba prolongada que reduce el NL pendiente; acumula energía y luego debe lanzar. No confundas Sabiduría (Dhar) 72 con Canalización 66 ni asignes una especialización que el perfil no concreta. El ritual final tiene su desarrollo narrativo propio: no se sustituye por una única tirada de lanzar un hechizo de combate.

Espada +7, BR 3 y sin armadura indicada, 15 Heridas. Para sobrevivir suele interesarle Esquivar o conservar distancia. Aplican Disfunciones e influencias corruptoras; sus poderes no le dan inmunidad automática.

Hallt, p. 13; números de lanzamiento contrastados con los registros de hechizos de Foundry. Perfil original de Foundry.

Anselm Buchberger · verdugo

Cuerpo a cuerpo (a dos manos) 63, Esquivar 56, Intimidar 67, Movimiento silencioso (rural) 56. Fuerza 47, Voluntad 45 para Frialdad sin avances. Gran hacha +10; BR 4, sin armadura publicada; 16 Heridas.

Asalto furioso 1: una vez por asalto, después de impactar en cuerpo a cuerpo puede gastar 1 Ventaja de Adversarios o el Movimiento aún disponible para un ataque adicional. En un éxito de ese ataque adicional, +1 NE por el talento. No tiene dos ataques gratuitos e incondicionales.

Ejemplo +0: primer ataque contra 63, un 32 da +3 NE. Si impacta, activa Asalto furioso: un 41 en el segundo da +2 NE y +1 del talento = +3 NE, antes de la defensa rival. No suma ese NE al primer ataque ordinario. La gran hacha tiene Traspasante, Impactante y Fatigante (llamado Fatigosa en la descripción del manual): limita Impactante al turno en que carga. Impactante suma las unidades del ataque al daño; no debe aplicarse sin más a todos sus golpes. Traspasante daña en 1 punto una pieza de armadura o escudo de la ubicación impactada. No confundirla con el hacha especial de Gismondo.

En la ventana, el objetivo atascado cuenta como Tumbado y le concede +20. Un ataque apuntado a la cabeza sigue aplicando su penalizador correspondiente. Disparo certero solo afecta a armas a distancia: no lo convierte en un ataque cuerpo a cuerpo sin penalizador.

Hallt, pp. 18–19; manual, Asalto furioso y Disparo certero. Perfil original de Foundry.

Diomira Kiefer · cetrera

Arco 63, Esquivar 51, Cuerpo a cuerpo (básico) 42, Movimiento silencioso (rural) 36, Poner trampas 48, Adiestrar animales 55, Carisma animal 39 y Criar animales 35. Percepción no entrenada usa Iniciativa 34.

Disparo rápido 1: con arma cargada puede disparar antes de que actúen los demás en el siguiente asalto; consume su Acción y Movimiento de ese turno. Aplica los modificadores normales, y +1 NE en un éxito por el talento. No es un disparo gratuito extra que se añade al turno completo.

Ejemplo +0: con Arco 63 y tirada 32 obtiene +3 NE; si es Disparo rápido, +4 NE. Con daño publicado del arco +4, son 8 de Daño antes de protección. Si causa Heridas sin enfrentamiento, genera 1 Ventaja, salvo que otro efecto impida generarla.

Experto en trampas 1: puede recibir una prueba de Percepción para advertir trampas sin declarar que las busca. +1 NE en éxitos al detectar trampas o usar Poner trampas: con 48 y tirada 25 obtiene +2 +1 = +3 NE. Una trampilla oculta no es automáticamente una trampa.

Puntería ya está en los valores publicados: usa Arco 63 sin sumarle otra vez +5. Recio ya está en sus 18 Heridas. Daga +3; Armadura 2 (6). Para manejar a Matabichos, elige Adiestrar animales, Carisma animal o Criar animales según esté enseñando, calmando o cuidando; no exige prueba por cada orden conocida.

Hallt, p. 22. El atributo HP del export difiere del PDF: aquí se utiliza el total de Arco 63 publicado en español. Perfil original de Foundry.

Matabichos · halcón de Diomira

HA publicada 25, Fuerza 15, Resistencia 25, Iniciativa 40, Agilidad 10, Voluntad 30, 7 Heridas. Ataque de garras +4; Percepción básica usa Iniciativa 40 cuando el DJ pida localizar algo.

Adiestrado (Domado, Casa, Guerra, Magia): vuelve a casa, está habituado al combate y a la magia. Guerra otorga +10 HA e ignora Asustadizo frente a ruidos fuertes: comprueba si el perfil preparado ya lo incluye. Los ejemplos mantienen la HA 25 impresa como referencia, sin sumar de nuevo bonificadores de preparación.

Pequeño: contra un humano Normal recibe +10 al impacto por ser menor. Ejemplo con la HA publicada: 25 +10 = 35, tirada 23: +1 NE, antes de defensa. Las garras causan +4 más el resultado del enfrentamiento; no vuelvas a añadir Fuerza.

Volar 100 es un valor de movimiento de vuelo, no una habilidad de ataque al 100. Asustadizo conserva sus desencadenantes no cubiertos por el adiestramiento. Bestial no le permite conversar ni razonar como un humano. No tiene talentos adicionales publicados.

Hallt, p. 22; manual, Adiestrado y Volar.

Ewald Auffarth · cantero

Oficio (cantero) 46, Aguante 63, Consumir alcohol 58, Cuerpo a cuerpo (básico) 35, Esquivar 65, Frialdad 36, Fuerza 48. Martillo +8, BR 4, sin armadura indicada; 14 Heridas.

Artesano (cantero) 1: +1 NE a un éxito de su Oficio asociado y sus beneficios de acceso/compra de avances. Buenas espaldas 1: añade 1 NE en Fuerza enfrentada y aumenta la capacidad de carga; también vincula éxitos de Remar y Nadar. No concede +10 a toda prueba de Fuerza. Muy fuerte es +5 permanente ya incluido: utiliza Fuerza 48.

Ejemplos +0: Oficio 46, tirada 23: +2 NE, más Artesano = +3 NE. Al empujar a alguien, Fuerza 48 y tirada 25 dan +2 NE, más Buenas espaldas = +3 NE para comparar con su rival. Esquivar 65 con 32 da +3 NE.

Como cantero puede valorar mampostería o interpretar el aprovechamiento de los hitos en el molino cuando una prueba resulte necesaria; la dificultad la determina el DJ. En combate, su Esquivar es mucho más fiable que su habilidad con el martillo.

Hallt, p. 22. Perfil original de Foundry.

Engendro del Caos · enfrentamiento final

HA 65, Fuerza 42, Resistencia 56, Iniciativa 23, Agilidad 24, 56 Heridas. Armadura 5 (10), Mordisco +7 y cuatro Tentáculos +5. Los valores de daño ya incluyen Fuerza.

Secuencia: dispone de su Acción normal y de cuatro ataques gratuitos, uno por tentáculo. Resuelve cada ataque y defensa. El rasgo Tentáculo puede enmarañar y agarrar al causar daño. Puede gastar 1 ficha de Adversarios para morder a todas las criaturas actualmente enmarañadas; esos mordiscos no generan más Ventaja.

Enorme contra tamaño Normal: Terror 2; daño ×2; Impactante; los impactos exitosos activan Golpe mortal según su regla. Quien defiende con Cuerpo a cuerpo sufre −4 NE; Esquivar evita ese penalizador. Los PJ menores tienen +10 al impacto. En Fuerza enfrentada, el engendro gana automáticamente contra criaturas dos tamaños menores: Golpear no es una vía ordinaria para tumbarlo.

Ejemplo completo: tentáculo 65, tirada 32: +3 NE. Otto esquiva con 40, tirada 51: −1 NE. Diferencia 4; daño del tentáculo 5 +4, más las unidades del 32 por Impactante (+2), todo multiplicado por tamaño: (5 +4 +2) ×2 = 22 antes de protección. No vuelvas a añadir BF 4 ni multipliques por tamaño una segunda vez.

Inmunidad a la Psicología impide asustarlo como a un humano; Sin dolor modifica sus respuestas a críticos; Corrupción (moderada) activa sus reglas de exposición. No inventes una tirada de Frialdad para hacerlo huir. Las condiciones especiales del perfil y Tamaño hacen que combatirlo sea muy peligroso: impedir el ritual es una solución real.

Hallt, p. 22; manual, rasgos de criatura, especialmente Tamaño. Perfil original de Foundry.

Lobos espectrales · peligro si permanecen al raso

Hallt remite a este perfil como posible peligro exterior; no exige un encuentro obligatorio. Manual, p. 329: HA 30, Fuerza 35, Resistencia 35, Iniciativa 30, Agilidad 30, Movimiento 9, 24 Heridas; Arma +6, Armadura 1.

Un ataque +0 con HA 30 y tirada 23 da +1 NE antes de oposición. Percepción básica puede usar Iniciativa 30; aplica Rastreador a la detección por olor según el rasgo. Tamaño Grande, Miedo 2, Zancada, Visión oscura, Muerto viviente y Constructo alteran persecución, detección y Psicología; no los trates como lobos vivos que se asustan con una amenaza ordinaria.

Inestable con Ventaja de Grupo: usa la versión revisada de ¡A las armas!, p. 135: al final del asalto se elige al azar una criatura Inestable y se compara la reserva de su bando con la enemiga; si la enemiga es mayor, pierde tantas Heridas como la diferencia, y se destruye definitivamente si llega a 0. La traducción dice «Adversarios» al nombrar la reserva opuesta; interpreta la comparación desde el bando de la criatura para evitar comparar una reserva consigo misma.

El export incluye rasgos opcionales: Corrompido (menor), Molesto, Infectado, Sin dolor y Territorial. Son opcionales en el manual: decide cuáles añades; no los atribuyas todos automáticamente al encuentro.

Hallt, p. 10; manual, p. 329; ¡A las armas!, p. 135. Perfil original de Foundry.

Personajes nombrados sin bloque de estadísticas

El suplemento no publica valores ni talentos para los siguientes personajes. Las habilidades son propuestas por su función, sin porcentaje inventado ni talentos supuestos. Si una escena exige oposición, el DJ debe preparar un perfil y fijar sus valores antes de tirar.

PersonajePruebas que pueden encajarLímite
Bertille Lindemann, jefa de la Guardia; guardias y cocheroPercepción, Intuición, Mando, Frialdad y Cuerpo a cuerpo para la Guardia; Conducir para el cochero.No se presupone Entrenado ni otros talentos militares. La muerte del cochero en el vuelco es un hecho de la escena.
Gerwine Brotzmann, posaderaCotilleo para noticias, Percepción para observar clientes y Regatear si hay negociación.Sus respuestas y el servicio ordinario no requieren una tirada por defecto.
Padre Lothar, sacerdoteTeología, Carisma y Consumir alcohol si resulta relevante.Ser sacerdote no concede automáticamente Bendecir, Invocar ni milagros concretos.
Gunter, plateroOficio (platero), Tasar y Regatear.No conoce la participación de Elva en la secta; su oficio no lo convierte en cómplice.
Linde Schenk, representante/zapatero según los pasajesHabilidades de trato o de su oficio solo si se desarrolla una escena propia.Conservar la discrepancia del texto; no hay perfil ni talento publicado que permita fijar una oposición numérica.
Ute Bott, Friedwart Hauptfehlt, Hunfried Mauss, Gerwin Schuhbeck, Aimar Harbutt y Griselda; otras víctimas y cabezasSu información llega por documentos, testimonios y las cabezas parlantes.No inventar tiradas, talentos o resistencia al interrogatorio de los muertos. Friedwart y el Gismondo superviviente son identidades narrativas distintas que comparten la historia del mismo cuerpo.

La entrada Ehrentraud Neuner pertenece a la tabla de Foundry. No se identifica con Hunfried ni se restaura la fila española duplicada que se eliminó del lector.

7. Fuentes y criterios de esta guía

  • El infierno cabalga hacia Hallt: PDF español, pp. 7–22 para escenas y perfiles; las 25 situaciones incluyen sus alternativas.
  • Manual básico: talentos, pp. 132–150; combate y movimiento, pp. 158–181; Corrupción, pp. 182–183; Psicología, pp. 190–191; magia, pp. 234–242; lobo espectral, p. 329; rasgos, pp. 338–343.
  • ¡A las armas!: Ventaja de Grupo, pp. 133–136, y talentos actualizados cuando corresponda.
  • Fichas del grupo: «Seis viajeros hacia Hallt», semilla 20261027; seis personajes iniciales, sin gastar sus PX disponibles.
  • Export de Foundry: los perfiles originales siguen enlazados y conservan su idioma. Se usa como fuente distinta, especialmente para los números de lanzamiento de Elva. No se han añadido PDF privados al sitio.

La ventana de Anselm, la etiqueta de dificultad del reloj, el tratamiento del adiestramiento y la redacción de Inestable se señalan donde afectan a la mesa. Los ejemplos no sustituyen las defensas, cualidades, estados o reglas especiales que correspondan a cada acción.

Anselm Buchberger

WSBSSTIAGDEXINTWPFEL
56284742434739254524

Anselm is a large brute of a man, clean-shaven, broken nose, dark-brown eyes, and a grim face, a few teeth missing, and a gold ring in his right ear. He wears the trappings of his guild — sombre robes, leather gloves and boots, and an executioner’s hood, which is pulled back when he is not on duty. He is not one for idle chatter, and is not inclined to speak, especially to those who endanger the cult. Grunting more than speaking, he attacks the Characters without hesitation, and without mercy.

Chaos Spawn

WSBSSTIAGDEXINTWPFEL
65None4256232427NoneNoneNone

The spawn is a mound of writhing flesh, chattering teeth, blinking eyes, and tentacles, all of which are moving and twisting.

Note: The Chaos Spawn has 4 free attacks — one for each tentacle. Successful hits may entangle the target. Once entangled, the creature may spend one Advantage to make a Bite attack against all creatures it has currently entangled. These attacks do not generate further Advantage.

Size: Remember that the Chaos Spawn's Enormous size means that it will inflict @Terror[2] on most average Characters, and @Terror[3] on Halflings. Additionally, its damage will be doubled against average Characters, and tripled against Halflings.

 

Items and abilities

  • Brass Penny
  • Gold Crown
  • Silver Shilling
  • 4 Tentacles
  • Size
  • Bestial
  • Immunity to Psychology
  • Armour
  • Bite
  • Fear
  • Painless
  • Corruption

      "system": {
        "description": {
          "type": "String",
          "label": "Description",
          "value": "<p>The creature has a number of tentacles equal to #.</p>\n            <ul>\n            <li>It gains one Free Attack Action per tentacle.</li>\n            <li>Each tentacle’s attack does Rating Damage, which includes its Strength Bonus already.</li>\n            <li>If it causes Damage, it can also give its opponent an Entangled Condition, which will initiate a Grapple between the target and that tentacle.\n            <ul>\n            <li>If a tentacle is Grappling, use the tentacle’s Free Attack Action to resolve that Grapple, not the creature’s Action </li>\n            </ul>\n            </li>\n            </ul>"
        },

      "flags": {
        "_sheetTab": {},

      "system": {
        "description": {
          "type": "String",
          "label": "Description",
          "value": "<p>The creature causes supernatural Fear in other creatures, with a rating equal to its Rating.</p>\n<p>The Fear trait represents an extreme aversion to something. Creatures that cause Fear have a Fear Rating; this value reﬂects the SL you are required to pass on an Extended Cool Test to overcome your Fear. You may continue to Test at the end of every round until your SL equals or surpasses the creature&rsquo;s Fear rating. Until you do this, you are subject to Fear.</p>\n<p>When subject to Fear, you suffer &ndash;1 SL on all Tests to affect the source of your fear. You may not move closer to whatever is causing Fear without passing a <strong>Challenging (+0) Cool</strong> Test. If it comes closer to you, you must pass a <strong>Challenging (+0) Cool</strong> Test, or gain a @Condition[Broken] Condition.</p>"
        },

          "type": "String",
          "label": "Description",
          "value": "<p style=\"margin: 0in; font-family: Calibri; font-size: 11.0pt; color: #231f20;\">This trait represents creatures whose size differ from the game standard (i.e. roughly human sized). There are seven steps of Size, ranging from Tiny to Monstrous.</p>\n<p style=\"margin: 0in; font-family: Calibri; font-size: 11.0pt; color: #231f20;\">&nbsp;</p>\n<div style=\"direction: ltr;\">\n<table style=\"direction: ltr; border-color: #a3a3a3; border-width: 1pt;\" title=\"\" border=\"1\" summary=\"\" cellspacing=\"0\" cellpadding=\"0\">\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td style=\"vertical-align: top; width: .868in; padding: 4pt 4pt 4pt 4pt; border: 1pt solid #A3A3A3;\">\n<p style=\"margin: 0in; font-family: Calibri; font-size: 11.0pt; color: #231f20;\"><span style=\"font-weight: bold;\">Size</span></p>\n</td>\n<td style=\"vertical-align: top; width: .868in; padding: 4pt 4pt 4pt 4pt; border: 1pt solid #A3A3A3;\">\n<p style=\"margin: 0in; font-family: Calibri; font-size: 11.0pt; color: #231f20;\">Tiny</p>\n</td>\n<td style=\"vertical-align: top; width: 2.0819in; padding: 4pt 4pt 4pt 4pt; border: 1pt solid #A3A3A3;\">\n<p style=\"margin: 0in; font-family: Calibri; font-size: 11.0pt; color: #231f20;\">Butterﬂy, Mouse, Pigeon</p>\n</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td style=\"vertical-align: top; width: .868in; padding: 4pt 4pt 4pt 4pt; border: 1pt solid #A3A3A3;\">\n<p style=\"margin: 0in; font-family: Calibri; font-size: 11.0pt; color: #231f20;\">Little</p>\n</td>\n<td style=\"vertical-align: top; width: 2.0819in; padding: 4pt 4pt 4pt 4pt; border: 1pt solid #A3A3A3;\">\n<p style=\"margin: 0in; font-family: Calibri; font-size: 11.0pt; color: #231f20;\">Cat, Hawk, Human Baby</p>\n</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td style=\"vertical-align: top; width: .868in; padding: 4pt 4pt 4pt 4pt; border: 1pt solid #A3A3A3;\">\n<p style=\"margin: 0in; font-family: Calibri; font-size: 11.0pt; color: #231f20;\">Small</p>\n</td>\n<td style=\"vertical-align: top; width: 2.1513in; padding: 4pt 4pt 4pt 4pt; border: 1pt solid #A3A3A3;\">\n<p style=\"margin: 0in; font-family: Calibri; font-size: 11.0pt; color: #231f20;\">Giant Rat, Halﬂing, Human Child</p>\n</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td style=\"vertical-align: top; width: .868in; padding: 4pt 4pt 4pt 4pt; border: 1pt solid #A3A3A3;\">\n<p style=\"margin: 0in; font-family: Calibri; font-size: 11.0pt; color: #231f20;\">Average</p>\n</td>\n<td style=\"vertical-align: top; width: 2.0819in; padding: 4pt 4pt 4pt 4pt; border: 1pt solid #A3A3A3;\">\n<p style=\"margin: 0in; font-family: Calibri; font-size: 11.0pt; color: #231f20;\">Dwarf, Elf, Human</p>\n</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td style=\"vertical-align: top; width: .868in; padding: 4pt 4pt 4pt 4pt; border: 1pt solid #A3A3A3;\">\n<p style=\"margin: 0in; font-family: Calibri; font-size: 11.0pt; color: #231f20;\">Large</p>\n</td>\n<td style=\"vertical-align: top; width: 2.0819in; padding: 4pt 4pt 4pt 4pt; border: 1pt solid #A3A3A3;\">\n<p style=\"margin: 0in; font-family: Calibri; font-size: 11.0pt; color: #231f20;\">Horse, Ogre, Troll</p>\n</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td style=\"vertical-align: top; width: .8875in; padding: 4pt 4pt 4pt 4pt; border: 1pt solid #A3A3A3;\">\n<p style=\"margin: 0in; font-family: Calibri; font-size: 11.0pt; color: #231f20;\">Enormous</p>\n</td>\n<td style=\"vertical-align: top; width: 2.0625in; padding: 4pt 4pt 4pt 4pt; border: 1pt solid #A3A3A3;\">\n<p style=\"margin: 0in; font-family: Calibri; font-size: 11.0pt; color: #231f20;\">Griffon, Wyvern, Manticore</p>\n</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td style=\"vertical-align: top; width: .8875in; padding: 4pt 4pt 4pt 4pt; border: 1pt solid #A3A3A3;\">\n<p style=\"margin: 0in; font-family: Calibri; font-size: 11.0pt; color: #231f20;\">Monstrous</p>\n</td>\n<td style=\"vertical-align: top; width: 2.1319in; padding: 4pt 4pt 4pt 4pt; border: 1pt solid #A3A3A3;\">\n<p style=\"margin: 0in; font-family: Calibri; font-size: 11.0pt; color: #231f20;\">Dragon, Giant, Greater Daemon</p>\n</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n</div>\n<p>&nbsp;</p>\n<h3>Using Size</h3>\n<p>&nbsp;</p>\n<p>if you wish to use size to make a creature bigger — for example converting a giant spider to a gigantic spider — then increase Strength and Toughness by +10 and reduce Agility by –5 per step of size you increase the creature. Reverse this if you wish to make a creature smaller&nbsp;</p>\n<p>&nbsp;</p>\n<p>&nbsp;</p>\n<h3>Size Combat Modifers</h3>\n<p>If larger:</p>\n<ul type=\"disc\">\n<li>Its weapons gain the Damaging Quality if the creature is one step larger, and Impact if two steps or more larger.</li>\n<li>It multiplies any Damage caused by the number of steps larger it is (so, 2 steps=×2, 3 steps =×3, and so on); this multiplication is calculated after all modifiers are applied.</li>\n<li>All successful strikes against smaller targets activate the Deathblow rule, even if the target survives.</li>\n</ul>\n<ul type=\"disc\">\n\n</ul>\n<p>&nbsp;</p>\n<p>If smaller:</p>\n<p>• It gains a bonus of +10 to hit.</p>\n<p>&nbsp;</p>\n<h3>Defending Against Big Creatures</h3>\n<p>You suffer a penalty of –2 SL for each step larger your opponent is when using Melee to defend an Opposed Test. It is recommended to dodge a Giant swinging a tree, not parry it!</p>\n<p>&nbsp;</p>\n\n<h3>Fear and Terror</h3>\n<p>If the creature is perceived to be aggressive, it causes Fear in any creature smaller than it, and Terror in any creature two or more steps smaller. The rating of the Fear or Terror equals the Size step difference. So, if the creature is Large, and its opponent is Small, it will cause Terror 2.</p>\n<p>&nbsp;</p>\n<h3>Moving in Combat</h3>\n<p>A creature that is larger ignores the need to Disengage if it wishes to leave melee combat; instead, it brushes smaller combatants out of the way, moving where it wishes.</p>\n<p>&nbsp;</p>\n<h3>Opposed Strength</h3>\n<p>During Opposed Strength Tests (and similar), if one creature is 2 or more size steps larger, it wins automatically. If one creature is 1 size step larger, the smaller creature must roll a Critical to contest the roll. If it does, SL are compared as normal. All other results mean the larger creature wins.</p>\n<p>&nbsp;</p>\n<h3>Stomp</h3>\n<p>Creatures that are larger than their opponents may make one Stomp as a Free Attack, by spending 1 Advantage, as they kick downwards or otherwise bash smaller opponents out of the way. This attack has a Damage equal to their Strength Bonus +0, and uses Melee(Brawling).</p>\n<p style=\"margin: 0in; font-family: Calibri; font-size: 11.0pt; color: #231f20;\">&nbsp;</p>\n<div style=\"direction: ltr;\">\n<table style=\"direction: ltr; border-collapse: collapse; border: 1pt solid #A3A3A3;\" title=\"\" border=\"1\" summary=\"\" cellspacing=\"0\" cellpadding=\"0\">\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td style=\"vertical-align: top; width: .8472in; padding: 4pt 4pt 4pt 4pt; border: 1pt solid #A3A3A3;\">\n<p style=\"margin: 0in; font-family: Calibri; font-size: 11.0pt; color: #231f20;\"><span style=\"font-weight: bold;\">Size </span></p>\n</td>\n<td style=\"vertical-align: top; width: .8472in; padding: 4pt 4pt 4pt 4pt; border: 1pt solid #A3A3A3;\">\n<p style=\"margin: 0in; font-family: Calibri; font-size: 11.0pt; color: #231f20;\">Tiny</p>\n</td>\n<td style=\"vertical-align: top; Diomira Kiefer

WSBSSTIAGDEXINTWPFEL
31533943342443273223

Diomira is a grim-faced woman, clad in dark leathers, and a cloak with a hood that she wears up to obscure her features. She bears scars on her face from when she was once attacked by a hunting bird, and wears many tokens of her hunts, such as feathers and teeth. Her face is grimy and her matted hair is tied back into a crude ponytail. When she speaks she has a gravelly tone, her voice better suited to the hushed words she speaks when hunting and commanding her falcons.

          "gmnotes": {
            "type": "String",
            "label": "GM Notes",
            "value": "<p>Diomira is a grim-faced woman, clad in dark leathers, and a cloak with a hood that she wears up to obscure her features. She bears scars on her face from when she was once attacked by a hunting bird, and wears many tokens of her hunts, such as feathers and teeth. Her face is grimy and her matted hair is tied back into a crude ponytail. When she speaks she has a gravelly tone, her voice better suited to the hushed words she speaks when hunting and commanding her falcons.</p>"
          },

      "name": "Fast Shot",
      "type": "talent",
      "img": "modules/wfrp4e-core/icons/talents/fast-shot.png",

      ],
      "flags": {
        "core": {}
      },
      "system": {
        "description": {
          "type": "String",
          "label": "Description",
          "value": "If you have a loaded ranged weapon, you can fire it outside the normal Initiative Order before any other combatant reacts in the following Round. You roll to hit using all the normal modifiers. Employing Fast Shot requires both your Action and Move for your upcoming turn, and these will count as having been spent when your next turn arrives. If two or more characters use Fast Shot, the character who has taken this Talent most goes first. If any characters have taken Fast Shot an equal number of times, both shots are fired simultaneously, and should both be handled at the same time"
        },
        "gmdescription": {
          "type": "String",
          "label": "Description",
          "value": ""
        },

Dire Wolf

WSBSSTIAGDEXINTWPFEL
300353530300000

When the earth gives up the dead, it is not just humans who rise; macabre parodies of Giant Wolves, with glowing eyes, and tatters of ﬂesh falling from their rotting, festering carcasses, Dire Wolves prowl the night on behalf of their necromantic masters. In the Reikland, they are said to roam the haunted forests of the Hägercrybs when Morrslieb is full, running wild in search of prey to sate their insatiable hunger, cursed with an appetite for ﬂesh and a heightened instinct for the smell of blood

      "name": "Unstable",

      "flags": {
        "_sheetTab": {},

      },
      "system": {
        "description": {
          "type": "String",
          "label": "Description",
          "value": "<p>The creature’s corpus is maintained by foul magics that are inherently unstable in the material realm.</p>\n<p>Whenever it ends a round engaged with any opponent with higher Advantage, the creature is driven back, and the magics holding it together weaken. It loses as many Wounds as the difference between its Advantage, and the highest Advantage engaged with it.</p>\n<p>So, if the creature had 1 Advantage, and its opponent had 3, the creature would lose 2 Wounds. If the creature ever reach 0 Wounds, the magics holding it in place collapse, and it ‘dies’.</p>"
        },
        "gmdescription": {
          "type": "String",
          "label": "Description",
          "value": ""

width: .8875in; padding: 4pt 4pt 4pt 4pt; border: 1pt solid #A3A3A3;\">\n<p style=\"margin: 0in; font-family: Calibri; font-size: 11.0pt; color: #231f20;\">Monstrous</p>\n</td>\n<td style=\"vertical-align: top; width: 2.1319in; padding: 4pt 4pt 4pt 4pt; border: 1pt solid #A3A3A3;\">\n<p style=\"margin: 0in; font-family: Calibri; font-size: 11.0pt; color: #231f20;\">Dragon, Giant, Greater Daemon</p>\n</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n</div>\n<p>&nbsp;</p>\n<h3>Using Size</h3>\n<p>&nbsp;</p>\n<p>if you wish to use size to make a creature bigger — for example converting a giant spider to a gigantic spider — then increase Strength and Toughness by +10 and reduce Agility by –5 per step of size you increase the creature. Reverse this if you wish to make a creature smaller&nbsp;</p>\n<p>&nbsp;</p>\n<p>&nbsp;</p>\n<h3>Size Combat Modifers</h3>\n<p>If larger:</p>\n<ul type=\"disc\">\n<li>Its weapons gain the Damaging Quality if the creature is one step larger, and Impact if two steps or more larger.</li>\n<li>It multiplies any Damage caused by the number of steps larger it is (so, 2 steps=×2, 3 steps =×3, and so on); this multiplication is calculated after all modifiers are applied.</li>\n<li>All successful strikes against smaller targets activate the Deathblow rule, even if the target survives.</li>\n</ul>\n<ul type=\"disc\">\n\n</ul>\n<p>&nbsp;</p>\n<p>If smaller:</p>\n<p>• It gains a bonus of +10 to hit.</p>\n<p>&nbsp;</p>\n<h3>Defending Against Big Creatures</h3>\n<p>You suffer a penalty of –2 SL for each step larger your opponent is when using Melee to defend an Opposed Test. It is recommended to dodge a Giant swinging a tree, not parry it!</p>\n<p>&nbsp;</p>\n\n<h3>Fear and Terror</h3>\n<p>If the creature is perceived to be aggressive, it causes Fear in any creature smaller than it, and Terror in any creature two or more steps smaller. The rating of the Fear or Terror equals the Size step difference. So, if the creature is Large, and its opponent is Small, it will cause Terror 2.</p>\n<p>&nbsp;</p>\n<h3>Moving in Combat</h3>\n<p>A creature that is larger ignores the need to Disengage if it wishes to leave melee combat; instead, it brushes smaller combatants out of the way, moving where it wishes.</p>\n<p>&nbsp;</p>\n<h3>Opposed Strength</h3>\n<p>During Opposed Strength Tests (and similar), if one creature is 2 or more size steps larger, it wins automatically. If one creature is 1 size step larger, the smaller creature must roll a Critical to contest the roll. If it does, SL are compared as normal. All other results mean the larger creature wins.</p>\n<p>&nbsp;</p>\n<h3>Stomp</h3>\n<p>Creatures that are larger than their opponents may make one Stomp as a Free Attack, by spending 1 Advantage, as they kick downwards or otherwise bash smaller opponents out of the way. This attack has a Damage equal to their Strength Bonus +0, and uses Melee(Brawling).</p>\n<p style=\"margin: 0in; font-family: Calibri; font-size: 11.0pt; color: #231f20;\">&nbsp;</p>\n<div style=\"direction: ltr;\">\n<table style=\"direction: ltr; border-collapse: collapse; border: 1pt solid #A3A3A3;\" title=\"\" border=\"1\" summary=\"\" cellspacing=\"0\" cellpadding=\"0\">\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td style=\"vertical-align: top; width: .8472in; padding: 4pt 4pt 4pt 4pt; border: 1pt solid #A3A3A3;\">\n<p style=\"margin: 0in; font-family: Calibri; font-size: 11.0pt; color: #231f20;\"><span style=\"font-weight: bold;\">Size </span></p>\n</td>\n<td style=\"vertical-align: top; width: 3.9312in; padding: 4pt 4pt 4pt 4pt; border: 1pt solid #A3A3A3;\">\n<p style=\"margin: 0in; font-family: Calibri; font-size: 11.0pt; color: #231f20;\"><span style=\"font-weight: bold;\">Wounds</span></p>\n</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td style=\"vertical-align: top; width: .8472in; padding: 4pt 4pt 4pt 4pt; border: 1pt solid #A3A3A3;\">\n<p style=\"margin: 0in; font-family: Calibri; font-size: 11.0pt; color: #231f20;\">Tiny</p>\n</td>\n<td style=\"vertical-align: top; width: 3.9312in; padding: 4pt 4pt 4pt 4pt; border: 1pt solid #A3A3A3;\">\n<p style=\"margin: 0in; font-family: Calibri; font-size: 11.0pt; color: #231f20;\">1</p>\n</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td style=\"vertical-align: top;       "system": {
        "description": {
          "type": "String",
          "label": "Description",
          "value": "<p>The creature causes supernatural Fear in other creatures, with a rating equal to its Rating.</p>\n<p>The Fear trait represents an extreme aversion to something. Creatures that cause Fear have a Fear Rating; this value reﬂects the SL you are required to pass on an Extended Cool Test to overcome your Fear. You may continue to Test at the end of every round until your SL equals or surpasses the creature&rsquo;s Fear rating. Until you do this, you are subject to Fear.</p>\n<p>When subject to Fear, you suffer &ndash;1 SL on all Tests to affect the source of your fear. You may not move closer to whatever is causing Fear without passing a <strong>Challenging (+0) Cool</strong> Test. If it comes closer to you, you must pass a <strong>Challenging (+0) Cool</strong> Test, or gain a @Condition[Broken] Condition.</p>"
        },

Elva Fellgiebel

WSBSSTIAGDEXINTWPFEL
46343231544349676142

Elva Fellgiebel is a striking  woman, wearing fine but functional garb, fitting her role as Reeve. She bears her badge of office with pride, and typically wears a wide-brimmed hat with a peacock feather set in place by a silver pin. She has a long face with thin lips and angular nose, framed by shoulder-length russet curls. Though her chin is raised with an air of haughtiness, her warm amber eyes are welcoming. Elva owns an opulent townhouse, is landlord to a number of local farmers, and she also owns the largest local brewery — Fellgiebel's Finest Fermentations. She is the cult leader and is being courted by Gunter, a cowering Silversmith who has no clue of his fianceé’s involvement with the cult. As the cult leader, Elva is skilled in some of the magical dark arts, and is also a knowledgeable alchemist.

          "gmnotes": {
            "type": "String",
            "label": "GM Notes",
            "value": "<p>Elva Fellgiebel is a striking&nbsp; woman, wearing fine but functional garb, fitting her role as Reeve. She bears her badge of office with pride, and typically wears a wide-brimmed hat with a peacock feather set in place by a silver pin. She has a long face with thin lips and angular nose, framed by shoulder-length russet curls. Though her chin is raised with an air of haughtiness, her warm amber eyes are welcoming. Elva owns an opulent townhouse, is landlord to a number of local farmers, and she also owns the largest local brewery &mdash; Fellgiebel's Finest Fermentations. She is the cult leader and is being courted by Gunter, a cowering Silversmith who has no clue of his fiance&eacute;&rsquo;s involvement with the cult. As the cult leader, Elva is skilled in some of the magical dark arts, and is also a knowledgeable alchemist.</p>"
          },

    "original": {
      "name": "Magic Shield (Daemonology)",
      "type": "spell",
      "img": "modules/wfrp4e-core/icons/spells/daemonology.png",
      "effects": [
        "g5xrHWYinn3mzhgZ"
      ],
      "flags": {
        "_sheetTab": {},
        "core": {}
      },
      "system": {
        "description": {
          "type": "String",
          "label": "Description",
          "value": "<p>You encase yourself in bands of protective magic. While the spell is active, add +Willpower Bonus SL to any dispel attempts you make.</p>"

    "source": {
      "kind": "module",
      "module_id": "wfrp4e-owb1",

    "source_sha256": "23fe24fd8c5d3c97304c030021d90b970030705dcf826346fa553154a35f71ad",
    "parent_record_id": "Compendium.wfrp4e-owb1.actors.Actor.i2b3ju0IwAsChPjH",
    "original": {
      "name": "Arcane Magic (Dark)",
      "type": "talent",
      "img": "modules/wfrp4e-core/icons/talents/arcane-magic.png",
      "effects": [],
      "flags": {
        "_sheetTab": {},
        "core": {}
      },
      "system": {
        "description": {
          "type": "String",
          "label": "Description",
          "value": "<p>You either study one of the 8 Arcane Lores of Magic — Beasts, Death, Fire, Heavens, Metal, Shadow, Light, or Life — or practice a lesser known Lore, such as Hedgecraft or Necromancy. You may now memorize spells from your chosen Lore for the following cost in XP.</p>\n<div>\n<table title=\"\" border=\"1\" summary=\"\" cellspacing=\"0\" cellpadding=\"0\">\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>\n<p>Number of Spells Currently Known</p>\n</td>\n<td>\n<p>XP Cost for a new spell</p>\n</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>\n<p>Intelligence Bonus × 1&nbsp;</p>\n</td>\n<td>\n<p>100 XP</p>\n</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>\n<p>Intelligence Bonus × 2</p>\n</td>\n<td>\n<p>200 XP</p>\n</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>\n<p>Intelligence Bonus × 3</p>\n</td>\n<td>\n<p>300 XP</p>\n</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>\n<p>Intelligence Bonus × 4</p>\n</td>\n<td>\n<p>400 XP</p>\n</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n</div>\n<p>&nbsp;...and so on.</p>\n<p>So, if your Intelligence Bonus is 4, it will cost you 100 XP for the first spell, and the next 4, then 200 XP for the next 4, and so on. Full rules for learning new spells are provided in @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.journals.YBVrpUHEjohB1H4f]{Magic}. Under normal circumstances, you may not learn more than one Arcane Magic (Lore) Talent. Further, you may not learn the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.items.QyjWtSdnVMT04l5Y]{Bless} or @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.items.voV0C2ar1bKpcpnH]{Invoke} Talents when you have the Arcane Magic Talent. You can unlearn this Talent for 100 XP, but will immediately lose all of your spells if you do so.</p>"
        },

          "label": "Description",
          "value": ""

      "system": {
        "description": {
          "type": "String",
          "label": "Description",
          "value": "<p>You channel a sickening ﬂow of <em>Dhar</em>, brieﬂy forcing a rent into the fabric of reality. A Lesser Daemon immediately manifests through the rent. Perform an <strong>Opposed Channel (Dhar)/Willpower</strong> Test with the Daemon. If successful, the Daemon will respond to one command issued by you, quite literally, then vanish (assuming the command is completed before the Duration ends). If failed, the Daemon immediately attacks.</p>"

      "system": {
        "description": {
          "type": "String",
          "label": "Description",
          "value": "<p style=\"margin: 0in; font-family: Calibri; font-size: 11.0pt;\">You have the spark to cast magic within you and have mastered techniques to control it at a basic level. When you take this Talent, you manifest, and permanently memorise, a number of spells equal to your Willpower Bonus. You can learn extra Petty spells for the following cost in XP.</p>\n  <p style=\"margin: 0in; font-family: Calibri; font-size: 11.0pt;\">&nbsp;</p>\n  <div style=\"direction: ltr;\">\n  <table style=\"direction: ltr; border-collapse: collapse; border: 1pt solid #A3A3A3;\" title=\"\" border=\"1\" summary=\"\" cellspacing=\"0\" cellpadding=\"0\">\n  <tbody>\n  <tr>\n  <td style=\"vertical-align: top; width: 2.4312in; padding: 4pt 4pt 4pt 4pt; border: 1pt solid #A3A3A3;\">\n  <p style=\"margin: 0in; font-family: Calibri; font-size: 11.0pt;\">No. of Petty Spells Currently Known</p>\n  </td>\n  <td style=\"vertical-align: top; width: 1.5833in; padding: 4pt 4pt 4pt 4pt; border: 1pt solid #A3A3A3;\">\n  <p style=\"margin: 0in; font-family: Calibri; font-size: 11.0pt;\"><span style=\"mso-spacerun: yes;\">&nbsp;</span>XP Cost for a new spell</p>\n  </td>\n  </tr>\n  <tr>\n  <td style=\"vertical-align: top; width: 2.4125in; padding: 4pt 4pt 4pt 4pt; border: 1pt solid #A3A3A3;\">\n  <p style=\"margin: 0in; font-family: Calibri; font-size: 11.0pt;\">Up to Willpower Bonus × 1</p>\n  </td>\n  <td style=\"vertical-align: top; width: 1.5333in; padding: 4pt 4pt 4pt 4pt; border: 1pt solid #A3A3A3;\">\n  <p style=\"margin: 0in; font-family: Calibri; font-size: 11.0pt;\">50 XP</p>\n  </td>\n  </tr>\n  <tr>\n  <td style=\"vertical-align: top; width: 2.4125in; padding: 4pt 4pt 4pt 4pt; border: 1pt solid #A3A3A3;\">\n  <p style=\"margin: 0in; font-family: Calibri; font-size: 11.0pt;\">Up to Willpower Bonus × 2</p>\n  </td>\n  <td style=\"vertical-align: top; width: 1.5333in; padding: 4pt 4pt 4pt 4pt; border: 1pt solid #A3A3A3;\">\n  <p style=\"margin: 0in; font-family: Calibri; font-size: 11.0pt;\">100 XP</p>\n  </td>\n  </tr>\n  <tr>\n  <td style=\"vertical-align: top; width: 2.4125in; padding: 4pt 4pt 4pt 4pt; border: 1pt solid #A3A3A3;\">\n  <p style=\"margin: 0in; font-family: Calibri; font-size: 11.0pt;\">Up to Willpower Bonus × 3</p>\n  </td>\n  <td style=\"vertical-align: top; width: 1.5333in; padding: 4pt 4pt 4pt 4pt; border: 1pt solid #A3A3A3;\">\n  <p style=\"margin: 0in; font-family: Calibri; font-size: 11.0pt;\">150 XP</p>\n  </td>\n  </tr>\n  <tr>\n  <td style=\"vertical-align: top; width: 2.4125in; padding: 4pt 4pt 4pt 4pt; border: 1pt solid #A3A3A3;\">\n  <p style=\"margin: 0in; font-family: Calibri; font-size: 11.0pt;\">Up to Willpower Bonus × 4</p>\n  </td>\n  <td style=\"vertical-align: top; width: 1.5333in; padding: 4pt 4pt 4pt 4pt; border: 1pt solid #A3A3A3;\">\n  <p style=\"margin: 0in; font-family: Calibri; font-size: 11.0pt;\">200 XP</p>\n  </td>\n  </tr>\n  </tbody>\n  </table>\n  </div>\n  <p style=\"margin: 0in; font-family: Calibri; font-size: 11.0pt;\">...and so on.</p>\n  <p style=\"margin: 0in; font-family: Calibri; font-size: 11.0pt;\">&nbsp;</p>\n  <p style=\"margin: 0in; font-family: Calibri; font-size: 11.0pt;\">So, if your Willpower Bonus is 3 and you had 3 Petty spells, it will cost you 50XP for the first learned spell, then 100 XP for the next three, and so on’.</p>"
        },

Ewald Auffarth

WSBSSTIAGDEXINTWPFEL
24224341322751322437

Ewald is a rugged man, with taught muscles, and a square jaw furnished with an unruly beard. His dust-caked clothing is simple and hard-wearing, with a simple metal pendant that bears the emblem of the Masonic Guild. He has already started to bald, and he is often seen smoking a pipe.

Gismondo

WSBSSTIAGDEXINTWPFEL
75426167473934434824

Hell Rides to Hallt

Though terrible and strange, fate has plans for the Headless Horseman of Hallt. He enjoys two Fate and two Fortune points. If possible, the GM should use these to keep him alive at least until the Characters reach the windmill.

This Actor uses a character sheet to accomodate for these points

The horseman wears armour that has been darkened and cast with grimacing faces — clearly the work of a fine blacksmith. He rides a large black warhorse, called ‘Hel’, and brandishes a sword and an executioner’s axe. Gismondo has a flair for the dramatic, and he has hidden several Incendiary Bombs inside some carved pumpkins. Once ignited, they emit a sulphurous gas and burst into flame mid-air. Gismondo’s voice sounds as if it is coming from inside almost hollow armour, a reverberating growl that rumbles through the night. In life, Hauptfehlt would often entertain his ‘brother’ Gismondo with poems and riddles. Now Gismondo has picked up the habit of speaking in rhyme or riddle, whenever possible, especially just after a murder.

          "biography": {
            "type": "String",
            "label": "Biography",
            "value": "<p>@UUID[JournalEntry.agdT9W0K6LgKs1XP]{Hell Rides to Hallt}</p><p>Though terrible and strange, fate has plans for the Headless Horseman of Hallt. He enjoys two Fate and two Fortune points. If possible, the GM should use these to keep him alive at least until the Characters reach the windmill.</p><blockquote class=\"foundry-note\"><p>This Actor uses a character sheet to accomodate for these points</p></blockquote><p>The horseman wears armour that has been darkened and cast with grimacing faces — clearly the work of a fine blacksmith. He rides a large black warhorse, called @UUID[Actor.6i69oQPSFvdPr7rp]{‘Hel’}, and brandishes a sword and an executioner’s axe. Gismondo has a flair for the dramatic, and he has hidden several Incendiary Bombs inside some carved pumpkins. Once ignited, they emit a sulphurous gas and burst into flame mid-air. Gismondo’s voice sounds as if it is coming from inside almost hollow armour, a reverberating growl that rumbles through the night. In life, Hauptfehlt would often entertain his ‘brother’ Gismondo with poems and riddles. Now Gismondo has picked up the habit of speaking in rhyme or riddle, whenever possible, especially just after a murder.</p>"
          },

    "source_sha256": "3e5d074140b988d1fcb080226c9abe268606f9e62995c671718d7282749ae47d",
    "parent_record_id": "Compendium.wfrp4e-owb1.actors.Actor.pDiCMkvXcPae8rsU",
    "original": {
      "name": "Dual Wielder",
      "type": "talent",
      "img": "modules/wfrp4e-core/icons/talents/dual-wielder.png",
      "effects": [
        "xIbjdXLXjt690zem"
      ],
      "flags": {
        "_sheetTab": {},
        "core": {}
      },
      "system": {
        "description": {
          "type": "String",
          "label": "Description",
          "value": "<p>When armed with two weapons, you may attack with both for your Action. Roll to hit with the weapon held in your primary hand. If you hit, determine Damage as normal, but remember to keep your dice roll, as you will use it again. If the first strike hits, once it is resolved, the weapon in your secondary hand can then target an available opponent of your choice using the same dice roll for the first strike, but reversed. So, if you rolled 34 to hit with the first weapon, you use 43 to hit with the second. Remember to modify this second roll by your off-hand penalty (–20 unless you have the Ambidextrous Talent). This second attack is Opposed with a new defending roll, and damage for this second strike is calculated as normal. The only exception to this is if you roll a Critical for your first strike. If this happens, use the roll on the Critical Table to also act as the roll for the second attack. So, if you scored a critical to the head and rolled 56 on the Critical table for a Major Eye Wound, your second attack would then strike out with a to-hit value of 56. If you choose to attack with both weapons, all your defensive rolls until the start of your next Turn suffer a penalty of –10. You do not gain an Advantage when you successfully strike or Wound an opponent when Dual Wielding unless both attacks hit.</p>"
        },

      "system": {
        "description": {
          "type": "String",
          "label": "Description",
          "value": "<p>The Horseman&rsquo;s Axe is a brutally efficient weapon, designed to sever heads with a single blow. Treat it as a @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.items.1zaqojk0Oq1m8vYv]{Hand Weapon} which enjoys the Impact quality when used from a raised position, such as from horseback, part way up a stairs, or when one&rsquo;s enemy has their head resting on a chopping block. If the axe scores a critical hit on a Character&rsquo;s head, roll twice on the critical hit table and choose the worst result.</p>"

        "description": {
          "type": "String",
          "label": "Description",
          "value": "<p>The Horseman&rsquo;s Axe is a brutally efficient weapon, designed to sever heads with a single blow. If the axe scores a critical hit on a Character&rsquo;s head, roll twice on the critical hit table and choose the worst result.</p>"

Goswin Samter

WSBSSTIAGDEXINTWPFEL
35353545303030505545

Goswin is a short, rotund, balding man, with light-grey hollow eyes, ruddy cheeks, and a crooked nose. Fond of commanding attention and displaying his wealth, he wears fine robes for his profession, with a thick fur coat to protect against the winter gales. He gesticulates while stressing his own importance, his hands displaying an array of expensive and garish rings. Between the trumpeting of his ruddy nose, phlegmy coughs and sips of his liquor, Goswin explains the legend of the ‘The Dullahan’, his eyes often darting about as another beast in the woods brays or caws.

        "description": {
          "type": "String",
          "label": "Description",
          "value": "<p>Laws vary considerably from one region to the next.       "system": {
        "description": {
          "type": "String",
          "label": "Description",
          "value": "<p>Called ‘opening your mouth and letting your belly rumble’ in Nordland, or simply ‘bullshitting’ in Ostland, blathering involves talking rapidly and incessantly, or talking volubly and at-length, about inconsequential or nonsense matters, and is used to verbally confuse and confound a target. You use your Charm Skill to Blather. Attempt an <strong>Opposed Charm/Intelligence</strong> Test. Success gives your opponent a Stunned&nbsp;Condition. Further, for each level you have in Blather, your opponent gains another Stunned Condition. Targets Stunned by Blather may do nothing other than stare at you dumbfounded as they try to catch-up with or understand what you are saying. Once the last Stunned Condition comes to an end, the target finally gets a word in, and may not be best pleased with you — after all, you have been talking about nothing or nonsense for some time. Should you stop talking, your opponent immediately loses all Stunned Conditions caused by your Blather. Generally, you can only attempt to Blather at a character once per scene, or perhaps longer as determined by the GM, as the target soon wises up to your antics.</p>\n<p>&nbsp;</p>"
        },
        "gmdescription": {

Hel

WSBSSTIAGDEXINTWPFEL
45None55451530None151510

Hel is a fine horse, and while stories abound about the terrible beast that carries the Horseman about the lands — that it is undead, or a daemon, or a mutant with seven nostrils and a lizard's tail — there is nothing supernatural about Hel. Gismodo 'liberated' her from a noble not far from Eilhart, and she has been his loyal comrade ever since.

Items and abilities

  • Brass Penny
  • Trained
  • Gold Crown
  • Silver Shilling
  • Size
  • Weapon
  • Stride
  • Armour

            "type": "String",
            "label": "Biography",
            "value": "<section id=\"secret-u0eKhOg6ZPeJCYF0\" class=\"secret\"><p>Hel is a fine horse, and while stories abound about the terrible beast that carries the @UUID[Actor.pDiCMkvXcPae8rsU]{Horseman} about the lands &mdash; that it is undead, or a daemon, or a mutant with seven nostrils and a lizard's tail &mdash; there is nothing supernatural about Hel.     "parent_record_id": "Compendium.wfrp4e-owb1.actors.Actor.6i69oQPSFvdPr7rp",
    "original": {
      "name": "Trained",
      "type": "trait",
      "img": "modules/wfrp4e-core/icons/traits/trait.png",
      "effects": [
        "ra1EGVf9mHjb4JrR"
      ],
      "flags": {
        "_sheetTab": {},
        "core": {}
      },
      "system": {
        "description": {
          "type": "String",
          "label": "Description",
          "value": "<p>This trait represents animals that have been trained through the Animal Training Skill. The skills the animal knows is marked in the brackets. Feel free to create your own trained skills.</p>\n        <p><strong>Broken</strong>: The animal is trained to ignore its Bestial trait. it receives [[/r 2d10]] Fellowship.</p>\n        <p><strong>Drive</strong>: The animal is trained to pull a coach, cart, plough, buggy, or similar.</p>\n        <p><strong>Entertain</strong>: The animal is trained to entertain others. It adds a +10 bonus to appropriate Entertain, Perform, or Play Tests.</p>\n        <p><strong>Fetch</strong>: The animal is trained to fetch. This is normal reserved for Dogs and similar.</p>\n        <p><strong>Guard</strong>: The animal is trained to stay in one place or prowl around as a guard, granting it the Territorial Trait.</p>\n        <p><strong> Home</strong>: The animal is trained to return home if it is released or lost.</p>\n        <p><strong>Magic</strong>: The animal is trained to ignore Skittish when it comes to magic, which is required for most horses used by Wizards.</p>\n        <p><strong>Mount</strong>: The animal will accept a rider. Some creatures are especially belligerent, and will not accept a rider without the correct skill. So, to ride a Griffon, you need the Ride (Griffon) skill.</p>\n        <p><strong>War</strong>: The animal is trained for war, gaining +10 Weapon Skill. It can also ignore Skittish for loud noises.</p>"
        },

        "description": {
          "type": "String",
          "label": "Description",
          "value": "<p style=\"margin: 0in; font-family: Calibri; font-size: 11.0pt; color: #231f20;\">This trait represents creatures whose size differ from the game standard (i.e. roughly human sized). There are seven steps of Size, ranging from Tiny to Monstrous.</p>\n<p style=\"margin: 0in; font-family: Calibri; font-size: 11.0pt; color: #231f20;\">&nbsp;</p>\n<div style=\"direction: ltr;\">\n<table style=\"direction: ltr; border-color: #a3a3a3; border-width: 1pt;\" title=\"\" border=\"1\" summary=\"\" cellspacing=\"0\" cellpadding=\"0\">\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td style=\"vertical-align: top; width: .868in; padding: 4pt 4pt 4pt 4pt; border: 1pt solid #A3A3A3;\">\n<p style=\"margin: 0in; font-family: Calibri; font-size: 11.0pt; color: #231f20;\"><span style=\"font-weight: bold;\">Size</span></p>\n</td>\n<td style=\"vertical-align: top; width: 2.0819in; padding: 4pt 4pt 4pt 4pt; border: 1pt solid #A3A3A3;\">\n<p style=\"margin: 0in; font-family: Calibri; font-size: 11.0pt; color: #231f20;\"><span style=\"font-weight: bold;\">&nbsp;Examples</span></p>\n</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td style=\"vertical-align: top; width: .868in; padding: 4pt 4pt 4pt 4pt; border: 1pt solid #A3A3A3;\">\n<p style=\"margin: 0in; font-family: Calibri; font-size: 11.0pt; color: #231f20;\">Tiny</p>\n</td>\n<td style=\"vertical-align: top; width: 2.0819in; padding: 4pt 4pt 4pt 4pt; border: 1pt solid #A3A3A3;\">\n<p style=\"margin: 0in; font-family: Calibri; font-size: 11.0pt; color: #231f20;\">Butterﬂy, Mouse, Pigeon</p>\n</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td style=\"vertical-align: top; width: .868in; padding: 4pt 4pt 4pt 4pt; border: 1pt solid #A3A3A3;\">\n<p style=\"margin: 0in; font-family: Calibri; font-size: 11.0pt; color: #231f20;\">Little</p>\n</td>\n<td style=\"vertical-align: top; width: 2.0819in; padding: 4pt 4pt 4pt 4pt; border: 1pt solid #A3A3A3;\">\n<p style=\"margin: 0in; font-family: Calibri; font-size: 11.0pt; color: #231f20;\">Cat, Hawk, Human Baby</p>\n</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td style=\"vertical-align: top; width: .868in; padding: 4pt 4pt 4pt 4pt; border: 1pt solid #A3A3A3;\">\n<p style=\"margin: 0in; font-family: Calibri; font-size: 11.0pt; color: #231f20;\">Small</p>\n</td>\n<td style=\"vertical-align: top; width: 2.1513in; padding: 4pt 4pt 4pt 4pt; border: 1pt solid #A3A3A3;\">\n<p style=\"margin: 0in; font-family: Calibri; font-size: 11.0pt; color: #231f20;\">Giant Rat, Halﬂing, Human Child</p>\n</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td style=\"vertical-align: top; width: .868in; padding: 4pt 4pt 4pt 4pt; border: 1pt solid #A3A3A3;\">\n<p style=\"margin: 0in; font-family: Calibri; font-size: 11.0pt; color: #231f20;\">Average</p>\n</td>\n<td style=\"vertical-align: top; width: 2.0819in; padding: 4pt 4pt 4pt 4pt; border: 1pt solid #A3A3A3;\">\n<p style=\"margin: 0in; font-family: Calibri; font-size: 11.0pt; color: #231f20;\">Dwarf, Elf, Human</p>\n</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td style=\"vertical-align: top; width: .868in; padding: 4pt 4pt 4pt 4pt; border: 1pt solid #A3A3A3;\">\n<p style=\"margin: 0in; font-family: Calibri; font-size: 11.0pt; color: #231f20;\">Large</p>\n</td>\n<td style=\"vertical-align: top; width: 2.0819in; padding: 4pt 4pt 4pt 4pt; border: 1pt solid #A3A3A3;\">\n<p style=\"margin: 0in; font-family: Calibri; font-size: 11.0pt; color: #231f20;\">Horse, Ogre, Troll</p>\n</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td style=\"vertical-align: top; width: .8875in; padding: 4pt 4pt 4pt 4pt; border: 1pt solid #A3A3A3;\">\n<p style=\"margin: 0in; font-family: Calibri; font-size: 11.0pt; color: #231f20;\">Enormous</p>\n</td>\n<td style=\"vertical-align: top; width: 2.0625in; padding: 4pt 4pt 4pt 4pt; border: 1pt solid #A3A3A3;\">\n<p style=\"margin: 0in; font-family: Calibri; font-size: 11.0pt; color: #231f20;\">Griffon, Wyvern, Manticore</p>\n</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td style=\"vertical-align: top; width: .8875in; padding: 4pt 4pt 4pt 4pt; border: 1pt solid #A3A3A3;\">\n<p style=\"margin: 0in; font-family: Calibri; font-size: 11.0pt; color: #231f20;\">Monstrous</p>\n</td>\n<td style=\"vertical-align: top; width: 2.1319in; padding: 4pt 4pt 4pt 4pt; border: 1pt solid #A3A3A3;\">\n<p style=\"margin: 0in; font-family: Calibri; font-size: 11.0pt; color: #231f20;\">Dragon, Giant, Greater Daemon</p>\n</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n</div>\n<p>&nbsp;</p>\n<h3>Using Size</h3>\n<p>&nbsp;</p>\n<p>if you wish to use size to make a creature bigger — for example converting a giant spider to a gigantic spider — then increase Strength and Toughness by +10 and reduce Agility by –5 per step of size you increase the creature. Reverse this if you wish to make a creature smaller&nbsp;</p>\n<p>&nbsp;</p>\n<p>&nbsp;</p>\n<h3>Size Combat Modifers</h3>\n<p>If larger:</p>\n<ul type=\"disc\">\n<li>Its weapons gain the Damaging Quality if the creature is one step larger, and Impact if two steps or more larger.</li>\n<li>It multiplies any Damage caused by the number of steps larger it is (so, 2 steps=×2, 3 steps =×3, and so on); this multiplication is calculated after all modifiers are applied.</li>\n<li>All successful strikes against smaller targets activate the Deathblow rule, even if the target survives.</li>\n</ul>\n<ul type=\"disc\">\n\n</ul>\n<p>&nbsp;</p>\n<p>If smaller:</p>\n<p>• It gains a bonus of +10 to hit.</p>\n<p>&nbsp;</p>\n<h3>Defending Against Big Creatures</h3>\n<p>You suffer a penalty of –2 SL for each step larger your opponent is when using Melee to defend an Opposed Test. It is recommended to dodge a Giant swinging a tree, not parry it!</p>\n<p>&nbsp;</p>\n\n<h3>Fear and Terror</h3>\n<p>If the creature is perceived to be aggressive, it causes Fear in any creature smaller than it, and Terror in any creature two or more steps smaller. The rating of the Fear or Terror equals the Size step difference. So, if the creature is Large, and its opponent is Small, it will cause Terror 2.</p>\n<p>&nbsp;</p>\n<h3>Moving in Combat</h3>\n<p>A creature that is larger ignores the need to Disengage if it wishes to leave melee combat; instead, it brushes smaller combatants out of the way, moving where it wishes.</p>\n<p>&nbsp;</p>\n<h3>Opposed Strength</h3>\n<p>During Opposed Strength Tests (and similar), if one creature is 2 or more size steps larger, it wins automatically. If one creature is 1 size step larger, the smaller creature must roll a Critical to contest the roll. If it does, SL are compared as normal. All other results mean the larger creature wins.</p>\n<p>&nbsp;</p>\n<h3>Stomp</h3>\n<p>Creatures that are larger than their opponents may make one Stomp as a Free Attack, by spending 1 Advantage, as they kick downwards or otherwise bash smaller opponents out of the way. This attack has a Damage equal to their Strength Bonus +0, and uses Melee(Brawling).</p>\n<p style=\"margin: 0in; font-family: Calibri; font-size: 11.0pt; color: #231f20;\">&nbsp;</p>\n<div style=\"direction: ltr;\">\n<table style=\"direction: ltr; border-collapse: collapse; border: 1pt solid #A3A3A3;\" title=\"\" border=\"1\" summary=\"\" cellspacing=\"0\" cellpadding=\"0\">\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td style=\"vertical-align: top; width: .8472in; padding: 4pt 4pt 4pt 4pt; border: 1pt solid #A3A3A3;\">\n<p style=\"margin: 0in; font-family: Calibri; font-size: 11.0pt; color: #231f20;\"><span style=\"font-weight: bold;\">Size </span></p>\n</td>\n<td style=\"vertical-align: top; width: 3.9312in; padding: 4pt 4pt 4pt 4pt; border: 1pt solid #A3A3A3;\">\n<p style=\"margin: 0in; font-family: Calibri; font-size: 11.0pt; color: #231f20;\"><span style=\"font-weight: bold;\">Wounds</span></p>\n</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td style=\"vertical-align: top; width: .8472in; padding: 4pt 4pt 4pt 4pt; border: 1pt solid #A3A3A3;\">\n<p style=\"margin: 0in; font-family: Calibri; font-size: 11.0pt; color: #231f20;\">Tiny</p>\n</td>\n<td style=\"vertical-align: top; width: 3.9312in; padding: 4pt 4pt 4pt 4pt; border: 1pt solid #A3A3A3;\">\n<p style=\"margin: 0in; font-family: Calibri; font-size: 11.0pt; color: #231f20;\">1</p>\n</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td style=\"vertical-align: top; width: .8472in; padding: 4pt 4pt 4pt 4pt; border: 1pt solid #A3A3A3;\">\n<p style=\"margin: 0in; font-family: Calibri; font-size: 11.0pt; color: #231f20;\">Little</p>\n</td>\n<td style=\"vertical-align: top; width: 3.9312in; padding: 4pt 4pt 4pt 4pt; border: 1pt solid #A3A3A3;\">\n<p style=\"margin: 0in; font-family: Calibri; font-size: 11.0pt; color: #231f20;\">Toughness Bonus</p>\n</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td style=\"vertical-align: top; width: .8472in; padding: 4pt 4pt 4pt 4pt; border: 1pt solid #A3A3A3;\">\n<p style=\"margin: 0in; font-family: Calibri; font-size: 11.0pt; color: #231f20;\">Small</p>\n</td>\n<td style=\"vertical-align: top; width: 3.9312in; padding: 4pt 4pt 4pt 4pt; border: 1pt solid #A3A3A3;\">\n<p style=\"margin: 0in; font-family: Calibri; font-size: 11.0pt; color: #231f20;\">(2×Toughness Bonus) + Willpower Bonus</p>\n</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td style=\"vertical-align: top; width: .8472in; padding: 4pt 4pt 4pt 4pt; border: 1pt solid #A3A3A3;\">\n<p style=\"margin: 0in; font-family: Calibri; font-size: 11.0pt; color: #231f20;\">Average</p>\n</td>\n<td style=\"vertical-align: top; Magical Sense

You are able to sense the Winds of Magic in others. You may attempt an Average (+20) Intuition Test whenever you encounter a spellcaster. If you pass, you sense the target is a witch. Further, if you score an Astounding Success (+6), can also determine the target’s highest Channeling Specialization.

Markolf Bachmaye

WSBSSTIAGDEXINTWPFEL
38294152303030354045

Characters asking after Bachmaye will find him in a back corner of The Calm Toad, drinking, singing, and behaving raucously. Even if they are not looking for the man, he may make himself known by loudly demanding more beer, ‘with a damn sight less water in it this time!’ He is happy to complain about life in general to anyone who is willing to listen, but ends each complaint with a laugh all the same, as though one could hardly expect much more from life than misery in any case. He has the ruddy-red complexion of someone who enjoys their drink, a portly physique, and gaudy, expensive-looking (if tatty) clothing. His hair is dirty brown in need of a cut, and his beard is wild and greying, also in need of a cut.

      "system": {
        "description": {
          "type": "String",
          "label": "Description",
          "value": "<p>At the age of 10, a Priest of Morr called a Doomsayer took you aside to foretell your death in an incense-laden, coming-of-age ritual called the Dooming. In conjunction with your GM, come up with a suitable Dooming. Should your character die in a fashion that matches your Dooming, your next character gains a bonus of half the total XP your dead character accrued during play.</p>\n<p>&nbsp;</p>\n<p><em>A stiff neck would serve thee</em></p>"

Night Vision

You can see very well in natural darkness. Assuming you have at least a faint source of light (such as starlight, moonlight, or bioluminescence) you can see clearly for 20 yards per level of Night Vision. Further, you can extend the effective illumination distance of any light sources by 20 yards per level of Night Vision.

Falling

When falling, you suffer [[/r 1d10 # Fall Damage]] Damage, plus 3 Damage for every yard you fall. Any suffered Damage is reduced by your Toughness Bonus, but not any Armour Points you may be wearing.

If you are purposefully falling — or, if you prefer, jumping downwards — you can attempt an Average (+20) Athletics Test to lessen the damage you may sustain. If successful, you count as having fallen 1 less yard, plus an extra yard less per SL scored.

If you reduce the distance you count as having fallen to 0 or less, you will suffer no Damage from the fall.

If more Wounds are suffered from a fall than your Toughness Bonus, you also gain the Prone Condition.

Exposure

Every 4 hours spent in a difficult environment — such as sub-zero temperatures, a hot desert, or a howling storm — requires you take an Endurance Test. Extreme environments require a Test every 2 hours.

Cold: Your first failure causes a penalty of –10 Ballistic Skill, Agility and Dexterity. The second failure reduces all other Characteristics by –10. Third and subsequent failures cause [[/r 1d10 # Damage]] Damage not modified by Armour Points, with a minimum of 1 Wound lost. If you reach zero Wounds, you immediately take an Unconscious condition. Certain Trappings provide bonuses and penalties to these Tests. See Clothing and Accessories and Miscellaneous Trappings.

Heat: Your first failure causes a penalty of –10 to Intelligence and Willpower, and adds a Fatigued Condition. The second failure reduces all other Characteristics by –10%, and adds another Fatigued Condition. Third and subsequent failures cause [[/r 1d10 # Damage]] Damage not modified by Armour Points, with a minimum of 1 Wound lost. Stripping off heavy Trappings cancels 1 failed test.

Broken

You are terrified, defeated, panicked, or otherwise convinced you are going to die. On your turn, your Move and Action must be used to run away as fast as possible until you are in a good hiding place beyond the sight of any enemy; then you can use your Action on a Skill that allows you to hide more effectively. You also receive a penalty of -10 to all Tests not involving running and hiding.

You cannot Test to rally from being Broken if you are Engaged with an enemy. If you are unengaged, at the end of each Round, you may attempt a Cool Test to remove a Broken Condition, with each SL removing an extra Broken Condition, and the Difficulty determined by the circumstances you currently find yourself: it is much easier to rally when hiding behind a barrel down an alleyway far from danger (Average +20) than it is when three steps from a slavering Daemon screaming for your blood (Very Hard -30).

If you spend a full Round in hiding out of line-of-sight of any enemy, you remove 1 Broken Condition.

Once all Broken Conditions are removed, gain 1 Fatigued Condition.

Fatigued

You are exhausted or stressed, and certainly in need of rest. You suffer a -10 penalty to all Tests. Removing a Fatigued Condition normally requires rest, a spell, or a divine effect, though in some instances, such as when a Fatigued Condition is caused by carrying too much (see Encumbrance), simply changing your circumstances (carrying fewer trappings, for example) can remove a Condition.

Prone

You have fallen to the ground, possibly because you have run out of Wounds, you've tripped, or because you've been hit by something rather large. On your turn, your Move can only be used to stand up or crawl at half your Movement in yards (note: if you have 0 Wounds remaining, you can only crawl). You suffer a -20 penalty to all Tests involving movement of any kind, and any opponent trying to strike you in Melee Combat gains +20 to hit you.

Unlike most other conditions, Prone does not stack — you are either Prone, or you are not. You lose the Prone Condition when you stand up.

Unconscious

You are knocked out, asleep, or otherwise insensible. You can do nothing on your turn and are completely unaware of your surroundings. Any Melee attack targeting you automatically hits on the location of the attacker's choice with the maximum possible SL it could score, and also inflicts a Critical Wound; or, if the GM prefers, any close combat hit simply kills you. Any ranged combat hit automatically does the same if the shooter is at Point Blank range.

The Unconscious Condition does not stack — you are either Unconscious, or you are not — so you do not collect multiple Unconscious Conditions.

Recovering from unconsciousness requires different circumstances depending upon why you fell unconscious. Refer to Injury for more on this. If you spend a Resolve point to remove an Unconscious condition, but have not resolved the cause of the incapacitation, you gain another Unconscious Condition at the end of the round. When you lose the Unconscious Condition, you gain the Prone and Fatigued Conditions
